        <meta property="og:description" content="Kerala Police have registered a criminal case against GLAS Trust Company LLC and others over allegations that a fabricated lender-authorisation letter was used to secure recognition of its ₹11,432.98-crore claim and 99.41% voting rights in the insolvency proceedings of Think &amp; Learn Private Limited, the company behind BYJU’S.FIR No. 0736/2026 was registered at Palarivattom Police Station, Ernakulam City, on October 20, 2026, under Sections 318(4), 336(3), 340(2), 61 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, covering allegations of cheating, forgery, use of forged documents and criminal conspiracy.The complaint was filed by Rajendran Vellappalath, Managing Director of Voizzit Technology Private Limited. The FIR names GLAS Trust, Sunil Thomas, a person recorded as “Ms Debra Aldres”, the identifiers “ARCHENG” and “WIWANG”, and other unidentified persons.At the centre of the complaint is a Direction Letter dated July 25, 2024, which GLAS Trust relied upon to establish its authority to represent lenders in the insolvency process. According to the petitioners' bench note submitted in Kerala High Court Review Petition No. 1228 of 2026, signatures from earlier documents were allegedly reused, while dates, lender details and amounts were altered to assemble the purported mandate.The bench note identifies twelve signature pages allegedly carrying a new date, three pages with changed amounts or lender details beneath unchanged signatures, six Redwood pages where amounts were reportedly inserted as comments, and sixteen additional pages containing reused signature images. The petitioners also contend that the assembled document was a Word file printed to PDF without electronic signatures. These allegations are yet to be established through investigation or judicial findings.The development comes amid Voizzit's ongoing review proceedings before the Kerala High Court. The court admitted its review petition on October 27, challenging an earlier June 12 judgment dismissing its plea for an investigation into alleged irregularities in the insolvency process. Following a difference of opinion between the two judges on interim relief during the October 29 hearing, the matter was referred to the Chief Justice for assignment to a third judge.The FIR brings the dispute over GLAS Trust's lender authorisation into the criminal-investigation process. The registration of the case does not, by itself, invalidate the claim or voting rights or halt BYJU’S insolvency proceedings.">

                <h1 class="title mb-1 lh-1">
                    BYJU’S Insolvency: Kerala Police probe alleged forgery in GLAS Trust’s ₹11,432-Crore lender mandate
                </h1>

                <div class="post_meta mb-2 mt-3">
                    	                	<a href="javascript:void(0);">
	                        <i class="fa fa-user"></i> 
	                        BW Online Bureau
	                    </a>
                	                    <span>

                </div>

                
                                    <div class="post-detail-tag mb-3 mt-3">
                        <div class="strap-text" style="background: #ededed; font-style: italic; font-weight: 600; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.5; padding: 15px;">
                            FIR follows allegations of reused signatures and altered lender details in a document linked to GLAS Trust’s 99.41% voting rights in the Committee of Creditors
                        </div>
                    </div>
                                
                                    <div class="post-detail-block-image">
                                                                                                                        <div class="mt-3">
                                        <img src="https://static.businessworld.in/1679596751_gszpcO_byjus_1200_1_.jpg" alt="">
                                    </div>
                                                              
                                                                   
                    </div>
                            </div> 

            
            <div class="post-text mb-3">
                <div class="ck-content">
                	<p>Kerala Police have registered a criminal case against GLAS Trust Company LLC and others over allegations that a fabricated lender-authorisation letter was used to secure recognition of its ₹11,432.98-crore claim and 99.41% voting rights in the insolvency proceedings of Think & Learn Private Limited, the company behind BYJU’S.</p><p>FIR No. 0736/2026 was registered at Palarivattom Police Station, Ernakulam City, on October 20, 2026, under Sections 318(4), 336(3), 340(2), 61 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, covering allegations of cheating, forgery, use of forged documents and criminal conspiracy.</p><p>The complaint was filed by Rajendran Vellappalath, Managing Director of Voizzit Technology Private Limited. The FIR names GLAS Trust, Sunil Thomas, a person recorded as “Ms Debra Aldres”, the identifiers “ARCHENG” and “WIWANG”, and other unidentified persons.</p><p>At the centre of the complaint is a Direction Letter dated July 25, 2024, which GLAS Trust relied upon to establish its authority to represent lenders in the insolvency process. According to the petitioners' bench note submitted in Kerala High Court Review Petition No. 1228 of 2026, signatures from earlier documents were allegedly reused, while dates, lender details and amounts were altered to assemble the purported mandate.</p><p>The bench note identifies twelve signature pages allegedly carrying a new date, three pages with changed amounts or lender details beneath unchanged signatures, six Redwood pages where amounts were reportedly inserted as comments, and sixteen additional pages containing reused signature images. The petitioners also contend that the assembled document was a Word file printed to PDF without electronic signatures. These allegations are yet to be established through investigation or judicial findings.</p><p>The development comes amid Voizzit's ongoing review proceedings before the Kerala High Court. The court admitted its review petition on October 27, challenging an earlier June 12 judgment dismissing its plea for an investigation into alleged irregularities in the insolvency process. Following a difference of opinion between the two judges on interim relief during the October 29 hearing, the matter was referred to the Chief Justice for assignment to a third judge.</p><p>The FIR brings the dispute over GLAS Trust's lender authorisation into the criminal-investigation process. The registration of the case does not, by itself, invalidate the claim or voting rights or halt BYJU’S insolvency proceedings.</p>

        function showTime(){
            var date = new Date();
            var h = date.getHours(); // 0 - 23
            var m = date.getMinutes(); // 0 - 59
            var s = date.getSeconds(); // 0 - 59
            var session = "AM";
            
            if(h == 0){
                h = 12;
            }

            if(h == 12){
                h = 12;
                session = "PM";
            }
            
            if(h > 12){
                h = h - 12;
                session = "PM";
            }
            
            h = (h < 10) ? "0" + h : h;
            m = (m < 10) ? "0" + m : m;
            s = (s < 10) ? "0" + s : s;
            
            var time = h + ":" + m + ":" + s + " " + session;
            document.getElementById("MyClockDisplay").innerText = time;
            document.getElementById("MyClockDisplay").textContent = time;            
            setTimeout(showTime, 1000);            
        }
        showTime();
